original: Simulation of coastal erosion at policy-relevant spatial scales necessarily involves significant simplification of hydrodynamic and sedimentary processes. Models employed in planning typically aggregate highly variable phenomena into parametric functions whose performance improves considerably in controlled settings but deteriorates when extended to heterogeneous field conditions. What emerges from critical examination of these approaches is something closer to a portrait of the models' sensitivities than a portrait of coastal systems themselves. The consequence is that predictions derived from such simulations require careful qualification when informing decisions about adaptation and defence.
